title: Delirium in hospital when you also have arthritis (UK)

direct_answer: Delirium is a sudden change in thinking, attention and alertness. It is common in older and frail people in hospital, especially after surgery or infection. Pain, dehydration, constipation, some medicines and unfamiliar surroundings can contribute. Tell staff quickly if you notice changes.

content:
Delirium is a medical emergency that can affect people with arthritis and frailty, particularly after a hip or knee operation or during an infection.

This guide explains the signs and how families can help. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Signs of delirium

  • Sudden confusion or difficulty concentrating.
  • Being more sleepy or withdrawn, or more restless and agitated.
  • Seeing or hearing things that are not there.
  • Symptoms that change during the day.

Risk factors

  • Older age and frailty.
  • Dementia or memory problems.
  • Surgery, such as joint replacement.
  • Infection, dehydration or constipation.
  • Uncontrolled pain.
  • Some medicines.

How families can help

  • Tell staff what the person is normally like.
  • Bring glasses, hearing aids and familiar items.
  • Help with drinking and eating.
  • Help the person know the time and date.
  • Encourage moving if safe.

Recovery

Delirium usually improves when the cause is treated, but it can take time. NICE recommends assessing people at risk and acting to prevent it.

When to get help

  • Call 999 if someone is very drowsy, hard to wake or has collapsed.
  • Get urgent help from NHS 111 or a GP if someone at home suddenly becomes confused.
  • Tell ward staff straight away if a patient's thinking suddenly changes.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Is delirium the same as dementia?

No. Delirium comes on suddenly and usually improves, though people with dementia are at higher risk.

Can delirium happen at home?

Yes. Seek urgent medical advice.

Sources and further reading

  • NICE CG103: Delirium
